Their excitatory output affects a wide area of the cortex and several subcortical nuclei. SPW-Rs occur during \"off-line\" states of the brain, associated with consummatory behaviors and non-REM sleep, and are influenced by numerous neurotransmitters and neuromodulators. They arise from the excitatory recurrent system of the CA3 region and the SPW-induced excitation brings about a fast network oscillation (ripple) in CA1. The spike content of SPW-Rs is temporally and spatially coordinated by a consortium of interneurons to replay fragments of waking neuronal sequences in a compressed format. SPW-Rs assist in transferring this compressed hippocampal representation to distributed circuits to support memory consolidation; selective disruption of SPW-Rs interferes with memory. Recently acquired and pre-existing information are combined during SPW-R replay to influence decisions, plan actions and, potentially, allow for creative thoughts. In addition to the widely studied contribution to memory, SPW-Rs may also affect endocrine function via activation of hypothalamic circuits. Alteration of the physiological mechanisms supporting SPW-Rs leads to their pathological conversion, \"p-ripples,\" which are a marker of epileptogenic tissue and can be observed in rodent models of schizophrenia and Alzheimer's Disease. Mechanisms for SPW-R genesis and function are discussed in this review.","affiliation":"The Neuroscience Institute, School of Medicine and Center for Neural Science, New York University, New York, New York.","publicationStatus":"ppublish","language":"eng","pubModel":"Print","pubTypeList":{"pubType":["Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't","research-article","Review","Research Support, U.S. Gov't, Non-P.H.S.","Journal Article","Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural"]},"grantsList":{"grant":[{"agency":"NINDS NIH HHS","acronym":"NS","grantId":"U01 NS090526","orderIn":0},{"agency":"NIMH NIH HHS","acronym":"MH","grantId":"R01 MH107396","orderIn":0},{"agency":"National Institutes of Health","grantId":"MH54671","orderIn":0},{"agency":"National Institutes of Health","grantId":"5U01NS090583","orderIn":0},{"agency":"NINDS NIH HHS","acronym":"NS","grantId":"NS075015","orderIn":0},{"agency":"NIBIB NIH HHS","acronym":"EB","grantId":"R21 EB019221","orderIn":0},{"agency":"NINDS NIH HHS","acronym":"NS","grantId":"5U01NS090583","orderIn":0},{"agency":"National Institutes of Health","grantId":"MH107396","orderIn":0},{"agency":"NIMH NIH HHS","acronym":"MH","grantId":"R01 MH102840","orderIn":0},{"agency":"NIMH NIH HHS","acronym":"MH","grantId":"MH107396","orderIn":0},{"agency":"NIMH NIH HHS","acronym":"MH","grantId":"MH54671","orderIn":0},{"agency":"NSF","grantId":"SBE 0542013","orderIn":0},{"agency":"National Institutes of Health","grantId":"NS075015","orderIn":0},{"agency":"NIMH NIH HHS","acronym":"MH","grantId":"R01 MH054671","orderIn":0},{"agency":"NINDS NIH HHS","acronym":"NS","grantId":"U01 NS090583","orderIn":0},{"agency":"Human Frontiers Science Program and the G.
